## Claims
- [source-backed] The 2011 paper states Conjecture 4.10: both Theorem 4.8 generating sets for \(J_{v_{r,s,t,n}}\) are minimal; it separately suspects \(M/\Lambda_+M\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\). [arxiv:0809.2981, lines 942-975]
- [source-backed] Candidate 2024 paper is Avery St. Dizier–Alexander Yong, *Presenting the cohomology of a Schubert variety: Proof of the minimality conjecture*, DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\); its supplied abstract says “We prove the minimality conjecture” using the Hopf algebra of symmetric functions. [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832]
- [unsupported] No supplied FULL-TEXT SOURCE block or theorem passage for DOI \(10.1112/jlms.12832\) gives its precise theorem, hypotheses, coefficient ring, or any integral indecomposables assertion. Thus the exact 2024 theorem-level target is not established.
- [proved] Minimality alone does not imply free integral indecomposables: for \(A=\mathbb Z[x]\), \(A_+=(x)\), and \(J=(2x,x^2)\), \((2x,x^2)\) is a minimal homogeneous generating set, but \(J/A_+J\cong\mathbb Z\oplus\mathbb Z/2\). Indeed, \(A_+J=(2x^2,x^3)\); the degree-one quotient is \(2\mathbb Zx\cong\mathbb Z\), and degree two is \(\mathbb Zx^2/2\mathbb Zx^2\cong\mathbb Z/2\).

## Strategy
Compared the 2011 full-text conjecture and stronger integral statement with the sole relevant 2024 candidate. Treated the 2024 abstract as metadata only, not theorem-level evidence.

## Gaps
The 2024 paper’s full theorem statement and hypotheses were not supplied. No inspected source establishes an implication from minimality to \(J_v/\Lambda_+J_v\cong\mathbb Z^{\binom{a+b}{a}}\).
